sources.title: José J. Gil, Polarimetric Characterization of Light and Media, author-revised 2020 version of Eur. Phys. J. Appl. Phys. 40 (2007)
sources.locator: §§2.1–2.6, PDF pp. 6–11 of the 85-page author-revised full text; coherency matrix, Stokes parameters, purity criterion, polarized-light quantities, mixed-state decompositions, physical invariants and degree of polarization.

contents.name: §2.1 The coherency matrix
contents.support: Supplies the classical two-component second-moment construction and explicitly distinguishes time averaging from ensemble averaging under stationary and ergodic assumptions. The local definition proves well-definedness from square-integrability, uses an explicitly declared ensemble, and does not import the source’s zero-mean analytic-signal assumption.

contents.name: §2.2 The Stokes parameters
contents.support: Provides the Hermitian-matrix Stokes-coordinate and positive-cone setting. The local statement fixes the S3 sign from its phasor convention and the proof derives the cone directly.

contents.name: §2.3 The purity criterion
contents.support: Provides the polarization purity/rank context. The local proof establishes the exact determinant and rank-one equality criterion without relying on the source’s purity formalism.

contents.name: §2.4 Physical quantities characterizing the polarized light
contents.support: Provides the intensity and normalized polarization-coordinate context. The authored theorem supplies its own definitions and does not identify the local mean-square field coordinate with calibrated irradiance.

contents.name: §2.5 Decomposition of mixed states
contents.support: Provides context that mixed classical polarization descriptions admit component decompositions. The assigned two-outcome ensemble is independently specified and its expectation is computed locally.

contents.name: §2.6 Physical invariants and degree of polarization
contents.support: Supports the degree-of-polarization and coherency-matrix viewpoint. The local proof establishes the normalized bound and states the zero-intensity domain boundary explicitly.

sources.title: Optics Lectures, University of Oxford, 2012, Lecture 2: Lenses and interference
sources.locator: §3.2 Coherence and §3.3 Interferometers, PDF pp. 9–10 of the complete 30-page lecture notes; slow-detector averaging, cross term, phase extrema and fringe visibility.

contents.name: §3.2 Coherence
contents.support: Derives the cross-correlation term in a two-field intensity model and defines normalized coherence using a slow time average. The local theorem instead uses an explicitly declared ensemble mean-square model and makes no time-average identification.

contents.name: §3.3 Interferometers
contents.support: Gives the two-field phase-extremized intensity and visibility formula. The local proof establishes the formula under a full unit-circle phase sweep and proves its bound through the coherency theorem.

sources.title: A. Hemmerich, Lectures on Classical Optics, Part III (2023)
sources.locator: PDF pp. 2–4 of the complete 29-page lecture notes: “The concept of coherence” and “Interference visibility.”

contents.name: The concept of coherence
contents.support: Records the mean-intensity cross moment for two fields and its long-time averaging convention. The local item declares an ensemble probability law rather than equating it with a temporal limit.

contents.name: Interference visibility
contents.support: Gives phase extrema and the normalized visibility in terms of the pair correlation, including equal-intensity special cases. The local proof covers unequal intensities and proves its own algebraic bound.

canonical.name: Finite two-outcome unpolarized ensemble with nonzero amplitude in each realization
canonical.support: The assigned example explicitly gives the probability space, two amplitudes, matrix entries and Stokes coordinates; source treatments motivate but do not replace this local computation.

canonical.name: Zero-intensity boundary of the normalized degree of polarization
canonical.support: The one-point zero-field ensemble makes S0=0, so the normalized quotient is outside its defined domain. This boundary counterexample is proved locally.
